prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-05-07. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.27 |
| Retained earnings       | -20,476M |
| Current liabilities     | 4,705M |
| Current assets          | 1,254M |
| Shareholders' equity    | -1,920M |
| Total liabilities       | 33,311M |
| Total assets            | 31,391M |
| EBIT / operating income | 465M |
| Revenue                 | 1,010M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-05-07, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows acute insolvency (negative equity of -$1.92B, negative retained earnings of -$20.5B, total liabilities > total assets) together with a critically impaired liquidity position (current ratio 0.27). Although positive EBIT exists, these metrics indicate an issuer that is highly vulnerable to default and already balance-sheet insolvent, mapping to the CC category on the 21-grade scale.
DECISION: CC
